subject: Clarify private deployment: EU data residency + VPC endpoint/IP mapping

Cc: Montrose Legal <legalops@montrose.io>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment questions — EU residency and VPC endpoints

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a short SIG/CAIQ follow-up focused on data residency and private connectivity for a potential Private deployment. Can you confirm the following at a technical level (we'll include this in our vendor packet):

- For an EU-hosted private deployment, do all application data, audit logs, and backups remain in EU regions (no cross-border snapshots by default)?
- What networking options do you support: VPC peering, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway? For each option please share the expected IP ranges we need to open on our firewall (or a CIDR reference).
- Key management: can we integrate a customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key)? If so, where are keys stored and is any key material ever exported to non-EU regions?
- Are there any control plane operations (upgrades, health checks) that require routing metadata or telemetry to US-based services?

We have attached the SIG starter doc. If it's easier, a short attestation PDF for EU residency would be appreciated.

Goal: collect the technical details this week so we can circulate to procurement.

Thanks,

Sylvia Park
Security Operations
Montrose Health
(sylvia@montrose.io)

Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — EU residency and VPC endpoints

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Logan (Solutions) and Kimberly (Security) for the specifics; below is a short summary and I attached a two-page factsheet that covers hosting options.

High-level answers:
- EU-only hosting: we can provision Private deployments that are restricted to EU regions (AWS eu-west-1 / eu-west-2, GCP europe-west). By default we do not move customer data out of the chosen region set.
- Networking: we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and Transit Gateway attachments. See the attached checklist with example endpoint names and the common CIDR ranges we advertise for peering.
- KMS: customer-managed keys are supported (BYOK). Keys can be kept in the customer's EU KMS/HSM; Redwood will never export raw key material.
- Control plane: control plane telemetry (deployment orchestration and build logs) is routed through our private control plane instances; these can be deployed in-region for Private installs. For hosted customers there is limited control plane metadata that touches our US control plane — for Private/VPC installs we can keep the control plane in-region per the package.

Next step: Logan, can you provide the specific CIDRs and the note about cross-region snapshot behavior? Kimberly, can you confirm the attestation wording we can share back to Montrose?

Best,

Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all — following up with the technical specifics Sylvia asked for. I tried to keep the notes concise; happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk the network team through this.

1) EU-only data residency
- For Private deployments (VPC + Private control plane), all at-rest data (object storage, DB snapshots) and audit logs are stored in the chosen region(s). We do not enable cross-region replication by default. Snapshots are retained per the customer's retention config; cross-region copy is opt-in and requires explicit config & approval.

2) Networking options & IP references
- VPC Peering: When peered, Redwood will advertise a short list of CIDR /28 blocks per deployment (example: 10.250.16.0/28, 10.250.16.16/28). These are per-deployment and can be customized if there's overlap with customer networks.
- AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints): we expose interface ENIs in customer subnets; no public IPs are used. Customers need to allow the Eni IPs which will be specific to the subnet. We provide a mapping file on deployment.
- Transit Gateway: supports large-scale connectivity; attachments use customer TGW route tables. No additional advertised public ranges required beyond the VPC CIDRs.

3) KMS / keys
- BYOK supported for AWS KMS & AWS CloudHSM, as well as GCP KMS. Keys are stored in the customer's KMS; Redwood requests a grant for use but we do not export key material. If customer requests HSM-backed keys, we can provide guidance on local key custody.

4) Control-plane metadata and telemetry
- For our Private package we can host the control plane in-region. There is an optional feature where some aggregated telemetry (anonymous metrics, feature usage) is sent to our central telemetry cluster — this is disabled for customers who require strict residency.

5) Attachments / artifacts we can provide
- EU residency attestation PDF (signed)
- SOC 2 system description excerpt that maps to hosting controls
- CIDR mapping file for the deployment (CSV)

Notes / caveats:
- If you choose a multi-region EU deployment for HA, there will be synchronous replication between EU regions only; no backup copies are sent outside the EU unless cross-region replication is explicitly configured.
- Managed upgrades may temporarily contact our code signing and artifact servers; for Private installs those servers can be mirrored to an in-region artifact repository.

If you want the CIDR list now I can generate the per-deployment /28s and a sample route table.
